title: Strict local fraction fields, normalization inertia, and split finite etale fibres
statement: Let $X$ be integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and normal, meaning that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Put $K=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ at the generic point and choose a separable closure $\Omega/K$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. Write $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$. For each $x\in X$, choose a strict henselization $A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ of $A_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with its structural map to $X$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Then $A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is a domain, and there exists a $K$-embedding $i_x:K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Frac}(A_x^{\mathrm{sh}})\hookrightarrow\Omega$ compatible with that structural map. For any such embedding set $J_x=\{g\in G:g|_{i_x(K_x^{\mathrm{sh}})}=1\}$. Any two compatible embeddings $i_x,j_x$ differ by an element $g\in G$, and $J_{x,j_x}=gJ_{x,i_x}g^{-1}$. For every finite etale cover $P\to X$ [def-galois-categories], its pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$; consequently $J_x$ acts trivially on $\operatorname{Hom}_K(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,P_K)$. For every nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, $A$ is an integrally closed domain with fraction field $K$. Let $C$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $\Omega$, namely the elements satisfying a monic polynomial over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For every prime $\mathfrak r\subset C$ lying over $x\in V$, put $I_{\mathfrak r}=\{g\in G:g\mathfrak r=\mathfrak r,\ g|_{\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak r)}=1\}$. Then $I_{\mathfrak r}$ is conjugate in $G$ to $J_x$, for any chosen compatible $i_x$. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], $K$ is the fraction field of every $A_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, through the structural germ map. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ has $A$ a domain with fraction field $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], its localizations $A_{\mathfrak p}$ are the corresponding stalks of $X$. They are normal domains by the hypothesis on $X$, so $A$ is a normal ring in [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Now [lem-weil-pbc-normal-ring-integrally-closed-total] makes $A$ integrally closed in $K$: for a domain the nonzerodivisors are exactly the nonzero elements, so the total ring of fractions is $K$. This proves the assertion about every nonempty affine open, and fixes the same $K$ in every subsequent local construction.

proof.text: Fix $x$. Let $B_x$ be the integral closure of the normal local domain $A_x$ in $\Omega$. The inclusion $A_x\subset B_x$ is injective and integral by its definition. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] there is a prime $\mathfrak q_x$ over $\mathfrak m_x$; it is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal]. A henselization of $A_x$ exists: [lem-per-ordinary-henselian-pointed-neighbourhood-limit], applied to the ring $A_x$ and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$, gives a henselian local $A_x$-algebra $H$ that is a directed colimit of separated etale finitely presented $A_x$-algebras $A_a$ with points over $\mathfrak m_x$ of residue field $\kappa(x)$, with $\mathfrak m_xH$ maximal; these are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-per-pointed-etale-limit-henselization], whose part (1) makes $H$ a henselization $A_x^{\mathrm h}$ of $(A_x)_{\mathfrak m_x}=A_x$ [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Let $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be the residue field of the prescribed $A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ (the separable closure of $\kappa(x)$ determined by its geometric point). By [lem-wf-strict-henselization-finite-lifts] the prescribed $A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is canonically $A_x$-isomorphic, respecting residues, to the colimit of finite local etale $H$-algebras $B_e$; transporting the $H$-algebra structure along this isomorphism makes $A_x^{\mathrm h}\to A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ a compatible henselization and strict henselization. Apply [lem-dl-a1-henselian-global-inertia-comparison] to $(A_x,K,\Omega,B_x,\mathfrak q_x)$ and this compatible pair $A_x^{\mathrm h}\to A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$. It states that $A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is a domain and supplies a compatible embedding $A_x\subset A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}\subset (B_x)_{\mathfrak q_x}\subset\Omega$. Extending to fractions gives a $K$-embedding $e_x:K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}\hookrightarrow\Omega$: $a/b$ maps to $e_x(a)e_x(b)^{-1}$, whose denominator is nonzero by injectivity. Its restriction to $A_x$ is the structural map fixed in Step 1. In particular $K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}/K$ is algebraic, since it embeds into the algebraic extension $\Omega/K$.

proof.text: Let $i,j:K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}\hookrightarrow\Omega$ be any two compatible $K$-embeddings. Put $E=i(K_x^{\mathrm{sh}})$ and define $f:E\to\Omega$ by $f(i(a))=j(a)$. This is a well-defined $K$-algebra embedding. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois], $\Omega/K$ is algebraic and normal, so every $K$-minimal polynomial of an element of $\Omega$ splits in $\Omega$. Apply [lem-exc-etale-embedding-extension-sepclosed] with base $K$, extension $\Omega$, intermediate field $E$, target $\Omega$ and map $f$. It gives a $K$-endomorphism $g$ of $\Omega$ extending $f$. By [lem-exc-etale-algebraic-endomorphism-bijective] this endomorphism is bijective, hence $g\in G$ and $j=g\circ i$. This argument applies to infinite $E/K$ as well as finite $E/K$.

proof.text: For $h\in G$, the condition $h\in J_{x,j}$ is $h(g(i(a)))=g(i(a))$ for all $a\in K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Applying $g^{-1}$ makes this equivalent to $g^{-1}hg\in J_{x,i}$. Thus $J_{x,j}=gJ_{x,i}g^{-1}$. Each $J_{x,i}$ is a subgroup because identities, products and inverses preserve pointwise fixing.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, comparison of choices in the setup; elementary stabilizer calculation

proof.text: Let $P\to X$ be finite etale and put $R=A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a),(b), $P_S=P\times_XS$ is finite over $S$ and affine, say $P_S=\operatorname{Spec}T$, with $T$ a finite $R$-module by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1), $P_S\to S$ is etale. The ring $R$ is local and strictly henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure]. By [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], it is henselian and $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$ is separably closed.

source.place: Tag 0BSM (lemma-local-exact-sequence-normal), trivial-composition paragraph; morphisms.tex Tags 01WL and 02GO (finite and etale base change)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-equivalence] to $R$. It makes $\overline T=T\otimes_Rk$ finite etale over $k$ and gives full faithfulness of reduction. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product], $\overline T$ is a finite product $\prod_{s=1}^n k_s$ of finite separable field extensions of $k$, allowing $n=0$. Each $k_s$ is $k$ by [lem-pc-sepclosed-finite-sep-trivial], hence $\overline T\cong k^n$. The finite etale $R$-algebra $R^n$ also reduces to $k^n$. Lift this residue isomorphism and its inverse by full faithfulness of the equivalence. Their composites reduce to the identity, so faithfulness makes the composites identities. Therefore $T\cong R^n$ as $R$-algebras. Taking spectra proves $P_S\cong\coprod_{s=1}^nS$. This includes the empty cover, for which $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BSM, splitting of Y^sh; algebra.tex Tag 04GK (lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale), Tag 00U4 (lemma-etale-at-prime)

proof.text: Write $L=K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Base change the decomposition in Step 6 to $\operatorname{Spec}L$. By [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-base-change-coproduct], it gives $P_K\times_K\operatorname{Spec}L\cong\coprod_{s=1}^n\operatorname{Spec}L$. Choose any embedding $i:L\to\Omega$. By the universal property of the fibre product, every $K$-morphism $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P_K$ has a unique lift over the fixed map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. The one-point spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ lands in exactly one summand, where the map is uniquely the fixed $L$-point, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Thus each $t$ is the scalar extension of the corresponding $L$-section of $P_K$. For $h\in J_{x,i}$, composing that section with $\operatorname{Spec}h$ leaves it unchanged because $h\circ i=i$. Hence $h$ fixes every $t$, proving triviality of the action; when $n=0$ the set is empty and the assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0BSM, first proof paragraph after normality: splitting after passage to the fraction field and triviality of the composite; expanded on geometric points

proof.text: Now fix $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and a prime $\mathfrak r\subset C$ over $\mathfrak p\subset A$ corresponding to $x$. Let $M=A\setminus\mathfrak p$. The affine stalk identification of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $A_x$ with $M^{-1}A$, compatibly inside $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], its integral closure in $\Omega$ is $B_x=M^{-1}C$ (since $M^{-1}\Omega=\Omega$). The prime $\mathfrak q=M^{-1}\mathfrak r$ lies over $\mathfrak m_x$, and is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal]. Its residue field is $\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak r)$: $B_x/\mathfrak q=M^{-1}(C/\mathfrak r)$ is a field containing $C/\mathfrak r$ and contained in its fraction field. Thus it is the full fraction field. Here no assumption that $x$ is closed in $V$ has been made.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, identification of inertia over arbitrary x with the local setup of Tag 0BSD; algebra.tex Tag 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize)

proof.text: Every $g\in G$ preserves $C$ and $B_x$: applying $g$ or $g^{-1}$ to a monic relation over $A$ or $A_x$ preserves that relation. Since $g$ fixes $M$, extension and contraction under localization show $g\mathfrak r=\mathfrak r$ if and only if $g\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q$. If these conditions hold, the induced actions on the fields in the identification $B_x/\mathfrak q=\operatorname{Frac}(C/\mathfrak r)$ agree: both send $\bar c/\bar s$ to $\overline{g(c)}/\bar s$. Thus the group $I_{\mathfrak r}$ in the item is exactly the local inertia group for $(A_x,B_x,\mathfrak q)$.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, first proof paragraph; localization and residue-action comparison written explicitly

proof.text: Apply [lem-dl-a1-henselian-global-inertia-comparison] with this particular maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ and the compatible pair $A_x^{\mathrm h}\to A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ constructed in Step 2. It supplies a compatible embedding $e:L=K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}\hookrightarrow\Omega$ for which the local inertia group is $\operatorname{Aut}_{e(L)}(\Omega)=J_{x,e}$. By Step 9 this is $I_{\mathfrak r}$. For any embedding $i$ chosen in the item, Steps 3 and 4 give $e=g\circ i$ and therefore $I_{\mathfrak r}=gJ_{x,i}g^{-1}$. The local comparison applies to arbitrary normal local domains, and the reduction equivalence and localization results likewise impose no Noetherian hypothesis. All conclusions of the item follow.
